statement: arc-14 (the enforcer-mechanization skeleton owner) had already implemented the SAME behavioral logic d01's owns-list assigns to src/parity.rs, but named the module src/oracle.rs (single-record accept_rule) and put its tests inline as #[cfg(test)] rather than under tests/scaffold.rs+tests/parity.rs. d01's actual gap versus what existed was: (1) a WHOLE-REGISTRY sweep (oracle.rs only proves one record against one supplied validator, never iterates a RuleRegistry), (2) the T3 label-presence gate, (3) the reverse-direction orphan check, (4) the two owns-listed integration test files plus tests/fixtures/{scaffold,parity}/** on disk.
why: A lane reading only its own workpack could assume a bare skeleton and duplicate scaffold_rule/accept_rule from scratch, colliding with arc-14 and violating the disjoint-files parallel-ownership premise the plan advertises. Reading the ACTUAL crate contents before writing (not just the workpack prose) was necessary to find the real gap.
howToApply: Before implementing any pack whose 'Where We Are' section describes a skeleton, Read every file already in the owning crate (not just grep for the module names the workpack lists) — a prior arc/lane may have shipped functionally-complete code under a DIFFERENT filename than your owns: list expects, and your real job is the delta (here: registry-wide sweep + T3 gate + orphan check + tests/ layout), not a re-implementation.

statement: enforcer-domain::paths::RelPath has no Default impl and its TryFrom<String> is the only constructor; workspace lint policy denies unwrap/expect/panic crate-wide (Cargo.toml [workspace.lints]: unwrap_used/expect_used/panic = deny), so a 'this string is structurally guaranteed to parse' fallback (e.g. building a diagnostic Finding::file from a fixed literal) cannot use .unwrap()/.expect() even when genuinely infallible.
why: First attempts (recursive retry, invented RelPath::default()/RelPath::from(String) methods that do not exist) were either unsound (infinite recursion on a hypothetical failure) or referenced nonexistent API. The correct pattern already has precedent in this workspace (enforcer-coordination, enforcer-lang-security): a narrowly scoped #[allow(clippy::expect_used)] directly on a function whose ONLY job is parsing one fixed, provably-valid literal, with a doc comment naming exactly why it cannot fail.
howToApply: When you need an infallible-in-practice conversion from a fixed literal into a validating newtype under a deny(unwrap_used/expect_used/panic) lint policy, grep the workspace first for '#[allow(clippy::expect_used)]' / '#[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]' precedent, then apply the same narrowly-scoped allow on a small dedicated function — do not invent fallback constructors on types you do not own, and do not use recursion as a fake-infallible guard.

statement: RuleRecord (enforcer-rules::registry) has no dedicated 'label' field for the T3 doctrine ('advisory, no mechanization possible + <reason>'); d01's parity module encodes the T3 label-presence gate as a check over RuleRecord.tags: a T3 record is accepted only if at least one tag STARTS WITH the exact prefix 'advisory, no mechanization possible' (T3_LABEL_PREFIX const in src/parity.rs), with the free-form '<reason>' appended after ' + '.
why: TEST_PROOF_EXPECTATIONS.md/RUST_ARCHITECTURE.md's doctrine requires the label's PRESENCE be T1-mechanically-enforced for every T3 row, but enforcer-rules (arc-04, out of d01's owns scope) does not carry a structured label field — tags is the only free-form carrier already on the record shape. Reusing tags avoids a cross-lane schema change to enforcer-rules that d01 does not own.
howToApply: Any sibling pack (d16-d18, d21-d23, d25-d28, h01-h08, etc.) authoring a genuine T3 rule row must put the verbatim string 'advisory, no mechanization possible + <concrete reason>' as one entry in that RuleRecord's tags array, or ParityOracle::sweep will flag it as missing the mandatory label even though no fixture/validator is required for T3.

statement: The ocentra-enforcer MCP server's coordination_claim/coordination_mail tools refused to write ('MCP server is stale... may write incompatible coordination events') because package.json's on-disk hash had drifted from the running server's startup snapshot. The documented fallback (ocentra_enforcer_run invoking scripts/rust-rules.mjs coordination <subcommand> --json) worked for 'claim', but the subcommand for sending a hub-wide message is 'message', not 'mail' -- 'coordination mail' returns exit 2 'unknown command: mail'.
why: The task briefing named the MCP tool ocentra_enforcer_coordination_mail, which internally likely maps to a CLI subcommand of a DIFFERENT name than the MCP tool's own name; blindly mirroring the MCP tool name as the CLI subcommand string in the fallback command array fails.
howToApply: When the primary coordination_* MCP tool is stale and you fall back to `ocentra_enforcer_run` + `scripts/rust-rules.mjs coordination <subcommand>`, do not assume `<subcommand>` equals the MCP tool's own suffix (e.g. `coordination_mail` -> `mail`); if the first guess 404s with 'unknown command', try `message` for the hub-wide send action before escalating.
